How it works

How a diffusion model generates video frames

time →
1. Noise
Start: random noise for all frames of the clip at once
→
time →
2. Step-by-step cleanup
The video is cut into pieces “place in frame × moment in time”. Dozens of steps remove noise; the text and the first frame guide every step
→
time →
3. Frames
24 frames per second that are consistent with each other, so motion looks smooth
There is no physics engine inside. The model has seen millions of videos and knows what motion usually looks like. So it fails where exact rules matter: hands and objects in contact, text, long scenes.
Schematic: frames from our shot 2, noise added for illustration.

Anti-pattern

Text-to-video, the whole story in one prompt: 4 failure types

text-to-videoVeo 3.1 • 8 s • text only
▶ video in the HTML version
Prompt (shortened)
Our friendly Glovo delivery courier enters a cozy Scandinavian cafe, … picks up a brown paper food delivery bag, puts it securely inside her turquoise backpack, then cuts to her riding a city bicycle through the rainy avenue at dusk … and then camera zooms in to a smartphone map …
00:02
Action skipped
the bag stays on the counter and never goes into the backpack
00:03
Details drift after the cut
the logo on the box changes: “Glono” → “Glovo”
00:05
Space breaks
handlebars with a phone slide in while the courier is still riding ahead
00:07
Pseudo-text
“Delivery Admest” instead of “Delivery Address”
Root cause: 3 scenes and 5 actions requested in 8 seconds.

Step 0 • storyboard

Storyboard: the whole story before the first generation

The story is split into shots of 4–8 seconds. Each row = one key frame + one prompt + one generation.
#FrameTimeActionCameraKey frame
10–8 sCourier takes the bag from the barista and turns to the exitmedium shot, slow push-inshot1_cafe_pickup.png
28–16 sRides a bicycle down a wet street at dusktracking alongside, low angleshot2_bike_rain.png
316–23 sThe route on the map draws itself to the destination pindigital push-in, slight tiltshot3_map_route.png
Full template (Creator Tools)
Shot / timingVisualVoice-overImage promptVideo promptSFXMusic
1 minute ≈ 8 shots of 8 s; 1 hour ≈ 450 shots. Keep the storyboard in a spreadsheet (Google Sheets, Excel): it is the work plan, the budget and the acceptance list at the same time.

Step 1 • references

Character sheet as the reference for every shot

  • A reference narrows the model’s choices for appearance.
  • Veo 3.1: up to 3 reference images. Kling 3.0: Elements, 2–4 images.
  • More stable, not guaranteed: review every shot.
Result: the same courier in shots 1 and 2.

Step 3 • prompt

Video prompt structure: 6 slots

1Camera
2Who
3Action
4Where & when
5Motion details
6Light
Shot 2 prompt (Veo 3.1, image-to-video)
Dynamic tracking shot moving forward alongside the courier. The same courier with short cropped curly hair pedals her bicycle forward through the rain-slicked city avenue at twilight. Wheels spinning smoothly forward with water spray cutting through shallow puddles. Wet cobblestones reflecting warm shop lights and streetlamps.
▶ video in the HTML version
Output: shot 2
  • Motion verbs (pedals, spinning, tracks): the model needs to know what changes.
  • Do not describe the frame again: it is already the input. One identifying detail is enough.
  • Describe what should happen. A negative prompt field exists only in some tools (Kling, Wan).

Step 3 • camera

Camera moves and the prompt terms for them

Locked-off cameraStatic
“static camera, locked-off shot”
Turn in placePan
“slow pan left across the street”
Tilt up / downTilt
“tilt up to the rooftops”
Move closer / awayDolly in / out
“slow dolly in to her face”
Move alongside the heroTracking
“tracking shot alongside the courier”
Circle around the subjectOrbit
“slow orbit around the mug”
Camera rises upCrane
“crane up over the street”
Handheld, slight shakeHandheld
“handheld, slight shake”
Models were trained on captioned video, so they understand camera terms. In chat apps you set the camera with words only; video studios also have dedicated controls (Runway, Kling, Luma).
Diagrams: top view (Pan, Dolly, Tracking, Orbit) and side view (Static, Tilt, Crane). Camera in blue, subject in yellow, motion as a green arrow.

Controls beyond the prompt: frames, extension, references

trajectory arrow:

Motion Brush (Kling): up to 6 selected elements, each with its own arrow, plus a static zone. Available on Kling 1.x–2.x models; not in the Kling 3.0 feature list.
First + last frame
The model fills in the motion between two images. Veo 3.1, Gemini Omni, Kling 3.0
Extend a clip
Veo 3.1: +7 s per step, up to 148 s (720p, not Lite)
Gemini Omni: +10 s per step, up to 40 s
Hero references
Veo 3.1 / Fast: up to 3 images, 8 s clip
Kling 3.0 Elements: 2–4 images

Step 5 • editing

Editing: three shots into one 23-second video

8 + 8 + 8 − 0.5 − 0.5 = 23 s
three Veo 3.1 clips and two transitions: a wipe and a fade through black
You can join clips in any editor (CapCut, DaVinci Resolve) or with one ffmpeg command. A person does the editing, not the model.

GenAI Basics • Lesson 05 • Video Generation15 / 21
Reference • google-genai

Gemini API: image-to-video in Python

import time
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

client = genai.Client()  # key from GEMINI_API_KEY
op = client.models.generate_videos(
    model="veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview",
    prompt="Tracking shot alongside the courier",
    image=types.Image.from_file(location="shot2.png"),
)
while not op.done:  # wait: ~11 s to ~6 min
    time.sleep(10)
    op = client.operations.get(op)
video = op.response.generated_videos[0].video
client.files.download(file=video)
video.save("shot2.mp4")
Long-running operation: submit → poll status → download. Generation takes seconds to minutes.

Generation cost: per clip, per minute, per hour of video

Priced per second of generated video, 720p. One hour of finished video = 3600 s = 450 shots of 8 seconds.
Model$ per second8 s clip1 minute1 hour1 hour, 3 takes per shot

Retakes multiply the budget. With 3 attempts per accepted shot you generate 3 hours of video to keep 1 hour.
Kling (web): 3.0, 1080p with audio = 12 credits/s, i.e. 43,200 credits per hour. Run drafts on Veo 3.1 Lite or Fast.
Prices: Gemini API and Runway API, October 2026; only successful generations are billed. Not included: key frame images, editing, audio, people’s time. 3 takes per shot is an assumption for the estimate.

Acceptance

Acceptance checklist for a generated clip

Even a good image-to-video clip gets a frame-by-frame review. Defects from our shots 2 and 3:
Shot 3, 1.5 seconds apart: the timer jumps 0:28 → 0:45, “Mep” instead of “Map”, the icon is a moped while the courier rides a bicycle.
Shot 2: the “THABIK” sign is random letters.
Acceptance checklist
  1. Hands and objects in contact: no merging or vanishing
  2. Text and numbers: readable and stable
  3. Face and clothes: match the reference
  4. Motion: speed and direction (wheels forward)
  5. First frame: matches the approved one
  6. Shot joins: light and colour match
The same checklist is the homework rubric.

Rights, labelling and provenance

Your own frames and characters
allowed, with an “AI-generated” label
Other brands, logos, styles
only with permission and after company lawyers review
Real people without consent
employees, clients, public figures: only with written consent
How a mark survives re-saving
Video from Veoand other Google models
→
SynthIDinvisible mark in the pixels
→
Re-encoding, cropping, screenshot
→
✓ usually survives
C2PAsignature in the file metadata
✗ easily lost
SynthID check: upload the video to the Gemini app (up to 100 MB, 90 s). It detects SynthID only; videos from other services may not be recognised.
EU AI Act, Art. 50: since 2 August 2026. 50(4): whoever publishes a deepfake must label it. 50(2): the model provider adds a machine-readable mark (systems released earlier: from 2 December 2026). Fines up to €15M or 3% of turnover.
